text: When an inner scope declares a name that already exists in an enclosing scope, the inner one hides the outer for the duration of the block. This is called ___ .
explanation: It is not always an error — a parameter named `x` shadowing a field named `x` is the ordinary case, and `this.x` reaches past it. It becomes a problem with fields, where Chapter 21 shows that declaring a field with an inherited name adds a second field rather than replacing the first, and which one you see depends on the declared type of the reference. Making fields private removes the possibility entirely.
